summary: Iter-26 frontend-only restructure validation: new /backup-dati dedicated page + sidebar entry + Azienda.jsx cleanup. 32/33 e2e Playwright assertions passed on the public preview URL. The new page renders cleanly with PageHeader, 4-card status strip, and all 4 sections (cloud snapshots, notifications, manual JSON backup, danger zone) with correct data-testids. Create→Restore-dialog→Delete cycle works; restore dialog is inline within CloudSnapshotsCard as required; notification chips add via Plus and Enter, remove via X, Salva persists (verified by reloading and chip count), Invia test returns the expected SMTP-stub toast 'Email registrate nel log (SMTP non configurato): 2'. Manual backup elements present; danger zone RESET gating + counters checkbox work. /azienda no longer contains danger-zone / cloud-snapshots-card / notification-settings testids — only the company anagrafica form + logo card. Sidebar gating works: logistica and contabilita see NO 'Backup & Dati' entry, and direct navigation to /backup-dati for non-admins is redirected to /dashboard (page not rendered). One bug found: the status strip 'Snapshot attivi' counter does NOT update after creating/deleting a snapshot — the cards stay at 0 even when rows appear in the table. Reason: StatusStrip useEffect has [] dependency and is a sibling of CloudSnapshotsCard so it never re-fetches. Mitigation: lift snapshot state to BackupDati, or pass a refresh signal/event to StatusStrip, or use a shared SWR/store. Cleanup performed: test notification chips removed, all created snapshots deleted, db.company.notifications back to {recipients: [], include_admin: true}.

ui_bugs.issue: 'Snapshot attivi', 'Ultimo backup', 'Spazio occupato' KPIs do NOT refresh after creating or deleting a snapshot. The StatusStrip component fetches /company/backup/cloud/list only once on mount (useEffect with []) and never re-fetches when CloudSnapshotsCard mutates the list. Verified by capturing strip text before (count=0) and after (count=0) a create that did add a row to the table. This violates the review-request line 'Status strip Snapshot attivi updates correctly after creating/deleting a snapshot'.

action_items: Fix StatusStrip to re-fetch (or receive snapshots via props) so the 4 KPI cards refresh after Crea snapshot / Trash. Simplest fix: lift `snapshots` state to BackupDati() and pass it down to both StatusStrip and CloudSnapshotsCard, OR expose a `reload` callback via context/ref.
critical_code_review_comments: BackupDati.jsx StatusStrip uses local fetch on mount only — duplicate API call with CloudSnapshotsCard (two GET /company/backup/cloud/list on first render). Consolidate into a single fetch and share state.
BackupDati.jsx imports many Phosphor icons that are unused on first scan (e.g., FloppyDisk imported then only used in NotificationCard — fine; but verify with eslint --no-unused). Not a blocker.

Manual restore reads file twice (once for preview, once on submit). For large JSON backups this duplicates parsing cost; could cache the parsed object in state when preview is built.

All interactive elements have data-testid — testability is excellent.

rca of the issue: StatusStrip and CloudSnapshotsCard are SIBLING components in BackupDati(). Each fetches /company/backup/cloud/list independently. CloudSnapshotsCard re-fetches after createNow/deleteSnap via its own load() callback, but StatusStrip is unaware of those mutations because its useEffect dependency array is [] (run-once). Reproduce: 1) login admin 2) open /backup-dati (strip shows count=0) 3) click 'Crea snapshot' 4) wait — a row appears in the table but the strip still shows 0 (Snapshot attivi), 'mai' (Ultimo backup), '0 B' (Spazio). Fix options (recommended order): (A) Lift snapshots state to BackupDati and pass snapshots+retention as props to both components — simplest, single source of truth, removes the duplicate GET on mount. (B) Add a context/event-emitter so CloudSnapshotsCard can ping StatusStrip after mutations. (C) Use SWR/React Query with key '/company/backup/cloud/list' and call mutate() after createNow/deleteSnap. Option A is ~15 lines of refactor.
